I'm preparing for a **Master of Science in Computer Science (MSCS)**. Rather than
jumping straight in, I'm building the foundation in four parallel tracks, all taken
online while working. This page keeps track of the plan for me, and it may serve as
a reference for anyone considering a similar path.

**Status key:** ✅ completed · 🟡 in progress · ⬜ planned

## At a glance

| Track | Program | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Computer science | Stanford — Foundations in Computer Science Graduate Certificate | 1 of 4 courses done |
| 2. Applied AI | Carnegie Mellon — AI Engineering Fundamentals Graduate Certificate | first course in progress |
| 3. Math foundations | University of North Dakota — calculus and discrete math courses | first course in progress |
| 4. Applied math for CS | Indiana University — Undergraduate Certificate in Applied Mathematics | planned |

## 1. Computer science track — Stanford

**Program:** [Foundations in Computer Science Graduate Certificate](https://online.stanford.edu/programs/foundations-computer-science-graduate-certificate),
Stanford Online. The core undergraduate CS sequence (systems, theory, algorithms,
and operating systems) that an MSCS program builds on. I'm taking the courses one at
a time, in this order:

| # | Course | Topic | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [CS107 — Computer Organization and Systems](https://online.stanford.edu/courses/cs107-computer-organization-and-systems) | how programs run on the machine: C, memory, data representation, assembly | ✅ completed |
| 2 | [CS161 — Design and Analysis of Algorithms](https://online.stanford.edu/courses/cs161-design-and-analysis-algorithms) | algorithm design paradigms and complexity analysis | ⬜ next |
| 3 | [CS103 — Mathematical Foundations of Computing](https://online.stanford.edu/courses/cs103-mathematical-foundations-computing) | proofs, discrete math, and the theory of computation | ⬜ planned |
| 4 | [CS111 — Operating Systems Principles](https://online.stanford.edu/courses/cs111-operating-systems-principles) | processes, concurrency, memory, and file systems | ⬜ planned |

## 2. Applied AI track — Carnegie Mellon

**Program:** [AI Engineering Fundamentals Graduate Certificate](https://www.cmu.edu/online/ai-engineering-fundamentals),
CMU College of Engineering. Graduate-level machine learning and deep learning,
taught in live online classes. It prepares me for graduate AI coursework and is
directly useful in my job.

| # | Course | Topic | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 24-887 — Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence for Engineers | supervised and unsupervised learning, model selection and optimization, introduction to deep learning | 🟡 in progress |
| 2 | 24-888 — Introduction to Deep Learning | CNNs, RNNs/LSTMs, GANs, applied to engineering problems | ⬜ planned |

My notes for this track: [Logistic Regression](notes/logistic-regression/index.qmd),
[Support Vector Machine](notes/support-vector-machine/index.qmd), and
[Neural Networks](notes/neural-networks/index.qmd).

## 3. Math foundations track — University of North Dakota

**Program:** individual self-paced [Enroll Anytime](https://und.edu/academics/online/enroll-anytime/math165.html)
courses from UND (not a certificate). The calculus sequence plus discrete
mathematics — the math that both the CS courses and the applied-math certificate
below assume.

| # | Course | Credits | Topic | Prerequisite | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Math 165 — Calculus I](https://und.edu/academics/online/enroll-anytime/math165.html) | 4 | limits, derivatives, integrals and their applications | placement or Math 107 | 🟡 in progress |
| 2 | [Math 166 — Calculus II](https://und.edu/academics/online/enroll-anytime/math166.html) | 4 | integration techniques, sequences and series, Taylor polynomials, parametric and polar curves | Math 165 | ⬜ planned |
| 3 | [Math 265 — Calculus III](https://und.edu/academics/online/enroll-anytime/math265.html) | 4 | multivariable calculus: partial derivatives, gradients, multiple integrals, vector calculus | Math 166 | ⬜ planned |
| 4 | [Math 208 — Discrete Mathematics](https://und.edu/academics/online/enroll-anytime/math208.html) | 3 | logic, proofs, induction, number theory, counting, recurrence relations | placement or Math 103/107/146/165 | ⬜ planned |

My notes for this track: [Calculus I (UND Math 165)](notes/calculus-1/index.qmd).

## 4. Applied math for computer science track — Indiana University

**Program:** [Undergraduate Certificate in Applied Mathematics](https://online.iu.edu/degrees/applied-mathematics.html),
IU Online (15 credits: four core courses plus one elective, 3 credits each). It goes
beyond calculus into the math used most in CS and machine learning: linear algebra,
differential equations, numerical methods, modeling, and probability. Calculus I–III
are prerequisites, which track 3 covers.

| # | Course | Role | Topic | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MATH-M 303 — Linear Algebra for Undergraduates | core | vectors, matrices, linear maps, eigenvalues | ⬜ planned |
| 2 | MATH-M 313 — Elementary Differential Equations with Applications | core | ordinary differential equations and their applications | ⬜ planned |
| 3 | MATH-M 371 — Elementary Computational Methods | core | numerical methods for solving math problems on a computer | ⬜ planned |
| 4 | MATH-M 447 — Mathematical Models and Applications | core | building and analyzing mathematical models | ⬜ planned |
| 5 | MATH-M 463 — Introduction to Probability Theory | elective | probability, random variables, distributions | ⬜ planned |

A few connections worth noting:

- **Calculus I → II → III** is a strict chain, and finishing it unlocks the IU
  certificate.
- **Discrete math (Math 208)** and **CS103** cover overlapping ground (logic, proofs,
  induction, counting) from a math and a CS angle. Doing both should make the proofs
  in **CS161** easier.
- **Linear algebra, probability, and multivariable calculus** are the math behind
  machine learning: gradients, matrices of weights, and probabilistic models all
  show up in the CMU courses.

## For anyone considering a similar path

- This is **my personal plan**, shaped by my background and goals. It isn't advice
  from any of these schools, and it doesn't guarantee admission anywhere. Check the
  requirements of the MSCS programs you're interested in.
- Course details, prerequisites, and availability change. Always confirm on the
  official program pages linked above.
- I record what I learn along the way in [these notes](index.qmd), which may help
  with some of the same courses.
